chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, on the authority of Musa ibn Umar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin'an, on the authority of Abi Sa'id al-Qamat, on the authority of someone who linked it up to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) established the alms-tax upon nine things and he forgave other things. They are: wheat, barley, dates, raisins, gold, silver, cows, sheep and camels. Someone asked, 'How about corn?' The Imam became angry and said, 'I swear by God that in the Prophet's lifetime sesame seeds, corn and birds' seeds were all available.' He was told, 'It is said that these did not exist at the time of the Prophet. That is why he has only established the alms-tax on those nine items.' The Imam became angry again and said, 'They lie. The Prophet's explicit order was to forgive everything else. One may only forgive what exists. I swear by God that the alms-tax has been made obligatory on nothing else but these nine things. Whoever wishes can accept it and anyone who doesn't wish can deny it and become an atheist.'

key_terms.تِسْعَة: nine (referring to the nine categories of zakat)

ai.seo_question: What are the nine specific items upon which zakat is obligatory according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to affirm the fixed nature of zakat categories (al-ashnab al-tis'ah) while clarifying the status of minor grains like sesame and millet, which were exempted rather than omitted due to absence. The Imam’s rebuke of those claiming these items were unknown during the Prophet's era underscores the distinction between historical presence and legal exemption, reinforcing the principle that zakat is strictly limited to these nine unless extended by analogy (qiyas) in later jurisprudence.
